claims.shortExcerpt: Soil Drainage: Good Drainage.
Male catkins hang all winter; bloom late winter to early spring on bare branches — temperate dormancy cue implied but no chill-hour figure published.
claims.transformation: Temperate nut crop with winter catkins → needsWinterChill=true (heuristic; no hour count).

claims.value: Both male and female flowers on the same plant; yellow-brown male catkins release pollen in late winter to early spring.
claims.shortExcerpt: Both male and female flowers can be found on this plant. They bloom in late winter to early spring on the still bare branches.

claims.value: Edible nuts ripen in late summer; clusters of 1–5 nuts released from husk when ripe.
claims.shortExcerpt: The fruit, in the form of a nut, is enclosed by a short leafy involucre… released from the husk in late summer when the nut has ripened.
Both male and female flowers can be found on this plant.
Monoecious with wind-pollinated catkins; named cultivars often need cross-pollination for best nut set — not explicitly stated on NCSU page.
claims.transformation: Commercial hazelnut production typically uses pollinizer cultivars.

claims.shortExcerpt: Wind-pollinated catkins; cross-pollination between compatible cultivars improves yield.
claims.transformation: Wind pollination + cultivar guidance → requires_pollinator=true (wind as vector).
